title: Safe When the World Shakes
overview: This song declares that God's presence keeps his people secure even when nature and nations fall into chaos.

parts.label: Unafraid in total chaos (vv. 1-3)
parts.note: The singer pictures the worst imaginable: solid mountains sliding into a raging sea, which in ancient imagery stood for chaos. Even then God is a shelter and a strength close at hand, so the singer refuses to fear.

parts.label: A river in God's city (vv. 4-5)
parts.note: The city is Jerusalem with its temple, which had no great river, so the gentle streams most likely picture God's presence bringing life and joy, in contrast to the roaring sea. God helps the city as morning comes, the moment night's danger ends; some readers link this to Isaiah 37, where the attacking Assyrian army's dead were found in the morning and its king then withdrew.

parts.label: Nations rage, God speaks (vv. 6-7)
parts.note: Whole kingdoms are in uproar, yet when God speaks, the earth melts. The refrain calls him the LORD of armies, meaning commander of heaven's forces, and the God of Jacob, tying this mighty God to Israel's ancestor and people.

parts.label: Come and see (vv. 8-9)
parts.note: Listeners are invited to look at real destruction God has brought, probably on armies that attacked his people, so this is not a gentle scene. Yet the ruin falls on war itself: bows and spears are broken and the remaining gear of battle burned (the Hebrew word may mean shields or war wagons) until fighting stops everywhere.

parts.label: Stop and know (vv. 10-11)
parts.note: The call to be still is closer to "Stop!" or "Let go!" and is likely spoken first to the warring nations, telling them to drop their weapons and recognize who is God. The song closes by repeating its confident refrain that this God is with us.

disagreement: Christians differ on whether the central call to be still is mainly a command to hostile nations to stop fighting or mainly an invitation to believers to rest calmly in God, and so whether the psalm is chiefly about God's victory or about inner peace.
think: When everything around you feels unstable, what do you find yourself leaning on, and how well does it hold?
